summary: Mount Kathleen fire lookout above Summerland, BC: built 1954, later dismantled; a snowmobile club shelter went up on the old foundation in the early 1990s.

facts.status_note: Tower dismantled; a snowmobile club shelter was built on the old foundation in the early 1990s, according to a hiking blog.

access.note: A hiking blog describes forestry and gravel roads from Peachland or Summerland. No source read names the land manager or describes gates or closures.

visit.trail_note: Most of the way up can be driven; hiking mostly follows ATV tracks, which the blog says suit a mountain bike.

events.note: Blog gives 1954 as the build year of the Kathleen fire lookout.

notes_for_editor: One detailed source: a personal blog whose text read here has no date. The build year and the dismantling come only from that blog. The Canada's Fire Lookouts index lists Kathleen by name only. The district (Regional District of Okanagan-Similkameen) comes from the record's BC base map point (TRIM symbol 30828), not from any text read, so the story leaves it out, since no text read names it. Search snippets from a YouTube video and a BC Forest Fire Lookouts Facebook group post (not readable in full here) say a fire may have burned the tower and mention 1993. They conflict with the blog's account of dismantling, so they were not used. Check them before publication. No source read describes the site today beyond the shelter's 1990s construction, and the blog does not say whether the shelter still stands. Access level 'public' rests on the blog's description of roads and carries no land-manager check.
